events.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet
events.summary: Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton submitted AlexNet to ILSVRC 2012 on September 30, 2012 — winning with 15.3% top-5 error and triggering the [deep learning] revolution.
events.about: AlexNet's [GPU]-trained convolutional network crushed traditional [computer vision] pipelines — convincing Google, Facebook, and industry to bet on [neural network]s. Hinton had pursued backprop for decades before this breakthrough.

narrative.whyChosen: AlexNet was the inflection point for modern [deep learning] adoption.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved [neural network]s could beat hand-engineered vision features at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: [Computer vision] relied on brittle handcrafted features that did not generalize.

events.title: iPhone 5 released
events.summary: Apple began selling the iPhone 5 on September 21, 2012 — taller 4-inch display, LTE, and the Lightning connector.
events.about: Lightning replaced the 30-pin dock connector — forcing accessory and hardware accessory developers to redesign. The taller screen broke the fixed 320×480 pt layout assumptions early iOS apps relied on, pushing Auto Layout adoption.

narrative.whyChosen: The iPhone 5 changed the iOS screen shape and connector standard overnight.
narrative.whyImportant: LTE and a new aspect ratio reshaped mobile layout and peripheral ecosystems.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers designed for a square-ish 3.5-inch canvas and a decade-old dock standard.

events.title: Samsung Galaxy Note II released
events.summary: Samsung released the Samsung Galaxy Note II — larger 5.5-inch screen and split-screen multitasking on [Android].
events.about: The Galaxy Note targeted stylus power users on [Android]. Larger 5.5-inch screen and split-screen multitasking on android. Note apps and split-screen [Android] development often targeted this hardware class.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy Note II advanced Samsung's stylus phablet line.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy Note hardware defined large-screen [Android] productivity for years.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] lacked a premium large-screen stylus flagship for note-taking workflows.

events.title: Joomla 3.0 released
events.summary: The Joomla project shipped Joomla 3.0 on September 27, 2012 — a Bootstrap-based admin [UI] and mobile-ready front-end templates.
events.about: Joomla 3 brought responsive templates, a modernized media manager, and improved ACL — aligning the CMS with mobile-first expectations. It followed the short-term release strategy before Joomla settled on longer support cycles in the 3.x era.

narrative.whyChosen: Joomla 3 modernized the admin experience with Bootstrap and responsive design.
narrative.whyImportant: It kept Joomla competitive as mobile traffic overtook desktop browsing.
narrative.problemSolved: Joomla 2.5's admin and default templates felt dated on phones and tablets.

events.title: Zoom video conferencing software launches
events.summary: Zoom Video Communications released its first software on September 10, 2012 — a cloud video meeting platform built by former WebEx engineers.
events.about: Zoom prioritized one-click joins and reliable screen share over enterprise telepresence complexity. Developers adopted it for standups, pair programming, and remote interviews long before COVID — then usage exploded in 2020 when offices closed. Its [API] and [SDK] powered embedded video in education and health apps.

narrative.whyChosen: Zoom became the default video layer for remote engineering teams.
narrative.whyImportant: Frictionless meetings made distributed standups and interviews routine.
narrative.problemSolved: Legacy WebEx and Skype calls were painful to join and dropped constantly.
